transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-04-07 16:00 PT
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Mateo Ruiz (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (Atlas Head of ML), Lina Gomez (Atlas Eng Manager), Ethan Chu (Atlas Infra)
Shared artifacts: Redwood benchmark spreadsheet (link), model catalog export (link), pilot run logs (s3://atlas/pilot-logs)

[00:00] Jordan Lee: Okay hi everyone, thanks for joining the weekly. Um quick roll call — can you hear me?
[00:06] Samir Patel: Yep, hear you Jordan, loud and clear.
[00:08] Lina Gomez: Yep.
[00:10] Jordan Lee: Great. So agenda — short results review from the 2k example set, model catalog comparison, pick a model to pin for the pilot and then discuss rollback/fallback policy. Priya will walk through the perf numbers.
[00:25] Priya Nair: Cool, thanks. I sent the updated spreadsheet, but quick highlights: we ran against the three candidates — redwood-model-2.1, redwood-model-2.1-quant, and rwr-2.0-extended (the older baseline). The quantized 2.1 gives about 2.4x token throughput improvement and about 32% cost reduction per token relative to the non-quantized 2.1. Latency p95 increased slightly for some long sequences when kv-cache misses occurred.
[00:55] Ethan Chu: Quick q — when you say kv-cache misses, are those from different user sessions or warmup? We saw a lot of cold starts in our infra during the first 5 minutes of the run.
[01:10] Priya Nair: Yeah, good call. The test included new session simulation to match real traffic shape, so first-request cold misses are present. We also did a warm-cache run — in warm-cache the p95 delta between quant and full was only about 40ms.
[01:30] Mateo Ruiz: Also note some tokenization differences — a few of the payment-specific prompts ended up longer token-wise on the quant variant, which inflated apparent latency. That may be more tokenizer mismatch than model slowdown.
[01:50] Lina Gomez: We flagged a couple of hallucination cases in the quant run — mostly when we forced shorter generation lengths for latency. Not sure if it's quantization or prompt truncation.
[02:05] Priya Nair: Understood. On quality metrics, rouge-like similarity dropped by roughly 1.8 points on average for quant versus full 2.1 for the curated KPI set. For our acceptance criteria (>= 92% similarity), quant is at ~90.2 so it's a small regression but noticeable.
[02:30] Samir Patel: That's the core — we care about those edge failures for regulatory copy (refund policies etc). If the model occasionally fabricates a refund amount, it's a non-starter.
[02:45] Jordan Lee: Totally. So possible options: 1) Pin quant 2.1 as primary for cost reasons but keep full 2.1 as auto-fallback for quality triggers, 2) Keep full 2.1 but use dynamic batching / autoscale to control cost, 3) Stagger by route — cheaper model for low-risk routes, full model for high-risk routes.
[03:10] Ethan Chu: Route-based pinning seems attractive but adds routing complexity on our side. Does Redwood support per-route pinning today?
[03:20] Priya Nair: Yes, Redwood supports per-route model policies; you can pin model at route level in the console. We also support automatic fallback policies based on a quality webhook or latency thresholds.
[03:34] Jordan Lee: I'll note though that webhook-based quality triggers will need you to define deterministic checks. For example if the generated refund amount doesn't match the transaction, that can trigger fallback.
[03:48] Lina Gomez: We can build that check. Samir — is that how you want to handle compliance-sensitive outputs?
[03:55] Samir Patel: Yes, a deterministic rule for monetary fields is ideal. We also want audit logs for any fallback invocations for SOC2.
[04:05] Priya Nair: Audit logs are part of Private/Dedicated tiers; hosted also has request logs but for longer retention Private gives you full control and KMS integrations.
[04:20] Samir Patel: Right — we're evaluating dedicated but want to see pilot economics first. If the quant variant saves ~30% cost but causes 1.8pt drop in QA, maybe fallback keeps us safe while still saving money overall.
[04:40] Mateo Ruiz: We also recommend a two-minute rolling window for automatic rollback decisions to avoid flapping — i.e., need N regression events within M minutes. Redwood has config knobs for that.
[04:55] Ethan Chu: Theo question — latency SLO is 350ms p95. Are those numbers with the q2.1 pin?
[05:03] Priya Nair: The 350ms p95 is achievable on dedicated capacity with proper batching; in the hosted cluster our p95 for quant pin was ~410ms under mixed traffic for the full 2k run. Warm-cache and dedicated reduced that to ~320ms.
[05:25] Lina Gomez: So we might need dedicated for production SLOs. Cost implications?
[05:30] Jordan Lee: We'll share the committed capacity vs hosted cost worksheet. For your current load estimates, dedicated looks to break even after ~3 months compared to hosted at peak. I'll attach the worksheet.
[05:44] Priya Nair: Back to model pinning — recommended pilot config: pin redwood-model-2.1-quant as primary for 70% traffic, full redwood-model-2.1 as fallback for quality webhook triggers, and route-based full-model for the /refunds route. Also enable prefix caching for repeated user histories.
[06:05] Samir Patel: 70/30 split — why not 90/10?
[06:10] Priya Nair: With 90/10 we see less data to detect regressions quickly; 70/30 gives a better balance of cost saving and signal for automatic rollback detection.
[06:20] Samir Patel: Okay fair.
[06:25] Jordan Lee: Any objections from engineering?
[06:28] Ethan Chu: We need to validate peering and throughput — and we want to run a dedicated throughput test to confirm p95 under sustained load.
[06:35] Lina Gomez: And provide the failing prompts list — I'll collate three canonical failing prompts (refund calc, address normalization, chargeback reason) and send them.
[06:44] Priya Nair: Great. Also we noticed one anomaly in the log: a tokenization mismatch causing extra tokens in Spanish-language prompts. Might be a tokenizer version mismatch between your preprocessing and our runtime. Please confirm tokenizer version.
[06:58] Samir Patel: We use tok v0.9.4 in prod. Does Redwood runtime use v0.9.4 or v0.9.6?
[07:06] Priya Nair: Runtime is at v0.9.5 currently; that could explain differences. We can run a quick tokenization parity job.
[07:15] Jordan Lee: Action: Priya to run kv-cache sensitivity and tokenization parity. Jordan to share pricing. Ethan to give VPC details. Lina to share failing prompts.
[07:28] Mateo Ruiz: Quick note on rollback implementation: you can choose soft fallback (send request to fallback model but still return primary if it succeeds) or hard fallback (return fallback output and drop primary). For compliance we typically recommend hard fallback for monetary fields.
[07:46] Samir Patel: Hard fallback for monetary fields, soft for others sounds good.
[07:52] Jordan Lee: On the catalog side, to be explicit: model ids in the plan are redwood-model-2.1 (full), redwood-model-2.1-quant (q8_0 style quant), rwr-2.0-extended (legacy). We'll pin the quant id in the pilot config.
[08:10] Lina Gomez: Will pinning lock us to a particular kernel/quantization config? If we pin to "redwood-model-2.1-quant" can Redwood swap an internal kernel update?
[08:20] Priya Nair: Pinning controls model version; we also support an immutable artifact id for strict pinning that prevents silent kernel swaps. If you want absolute reproducibility, request immutable pinning and we'll produce an artifact checksum.
[08:34] Ethan Chu: Good to know. For the pilot, we want reproducibility but also easy patching. Is there a rollback window?
[08:42] Mateo Ruiz: Rollbacks can be immediate. We also support gradual rollbacks via canary percentages automatically.
[08:48] Jordan Lee: All right, let's capture agreements: pin redwood-model-2.1-quant as primary for pilot at 70% traffic; full model fallback for quality triggers and route-based full model for /refunds. Run dedicated throughput test 2025-04-15. Redwood to share benchmark spreadsheet and pricing by 2025-04-10. Atlas to provide failing prompts and VPC details by 2025-04-09.
[09:10] Samir Patel: Sounds good.
[09:13] Lina Gomez: One more operational question — what telemetry do you expose for fallback events?
[09:19] Priya Nair: We provide per-request metadata showing model chosen, fallback reason, latency, and an event stream for fallback events that can be exported to your SIEM. That stream includes the request id and model ids.
[09:32] Ethan Chu: Will we be able to correlate that with our logs?
[09:34] Priya Nair: Yes, request id is consistent across the call and can be sent in the x-redwood-request header so you can join logs.
[09:42] Jordan Lee: Okay if there are no further items we'll wrap. Thanks everyone. We'll follow up in the thread with the spreadsheet and test slots.
[09:52] Samir Patel: Thanks.
[09:56] Lina Gomez: Thanks all.

End transcript.
